foilCalibration.brightnessSequence: Keep the card still: LEDs off > white 4/255 > white 12/255 > white 4/255 > white 12/255 > LEDs off. Each state waits at least 1 second after acknowledgement. Ambient, dim and brighter white are each captured twice, with separate stability checks. Off means ambient light, not darkness. No automatic foil decision is made.
foilCalibration.brightComparison: Repeated brighter white (12/255): intensity shift {{shift}} points; normalized difference {{difference}}%; corner shift {{movement}}% of frame diagonal.
foilCalibration.ambientComparison: Repeated ambient: intensity shift {{shift}} points; normalized difference {{difference}}%; corner shift {{movement}}% of frame diagonal.
foilCalibration.ambientHelp: Ambient comparison estimates a separate median lighting gain per RGB channel, then measures remaining positive and negative changes on aligned card pixels. Dark, saturated and predicted-saturated pixels are excluded. At least 25% usable pixels and corner shifts no greater than 1% of the frame diagonal are required. This reduces simple artwork/exposure effects but cannot remove all of them. Values are experimental, not foil confidence; check capture warnings.
foilCalibration.ambientMetrics: Ambient residual ({{eligible}}% usable): positive mean {{mean}} points, 99th percentile {{peak}} points, negative mean {{negative}} points.
foilCalibration.ambientUnavailable: Ambient comparison unavailable: missing crop, excessive corner shift, or too few usable channel/pixel values. No foil inference.
foilCalibration.reflectionHelp: Spot measurements compare a 3x3 center to a surrounding 13x13 ring. Candidates need at least 55% intensity and 20 points of local contrast. Components need 3 pixels; box fill describes shape. Printed artwork also creates spots. Initial foil and non-foil results overlap: more spots or stronger contrast does not mean foil.
foilCalibration.reflections: Local contrast (99.9th percentile): {{contrast}} points; {{count}} spots, {{area}}% candidate area; largest {{largest}}%, box fill {{compactness}}%. Experimental, not a foil score.
foilCalibration.brightnessHelp: Applied only when capturing, not saved as a sorter setting. Start at 48 for the next test (previous captures used 96).
foilCalibration.analysisFailed: Card analysis failed. Your captured photos remain saved. Check model availability and browser storage, then retry Analyze card area.
foilCalibration.analysisHelp: Detected card crops exclude a 6% edge margin from measurements. Highlights are pixels above both 60% intensity and the card median plus 25 percentage points. Quality limits are experimental diagnostics, not a foil classifier or an accuracy guarantee. Inspect the crops for incorrect corner detection.
foilCalibration.whiteComparison: Repeated white: intensity shift {{shift}} percentage points; brightness-normalized difference {{difference}}%; corner shift {{movement}}% of frame diagonal.

quality.brightUnstable: Repeated brighter-white comparison is unavailable or exceeds an existing exposure, alignment or image-difference limit. Check phone exposure, movement and card crops before interpreting the brightness experiment.
quality.ambientUnstable: Repeated ambient comparison is unavailable or exceeds an existing exposure, alignment or image-difference limit. Check ambient light, phone exposure and movement before interpreting the brightness experiment.
quality.missingCard: Card detection was unavailable or its corners shifted more than 3% of the frame diagonal from the reference. Inconsistent crops are not measured. No complete quality assessment is possible.
quality.clipping: More than 2% of a card crop reaches intensity 250/255 in at least one channel. Try lower capture brightness.
quality.exposure: Repeated white intensity changes by more than 5 percentage points. Exposure or lighting may not have settled.
quality.movement: Repeated white corners shift by more than 1% of the frame diagonal. Movement or inconsistent corner detection may affect comparison.
quality.unstable: Repeated white crops differ by more than 4% after brightness normalization. Check movement, exposure and detection.
quality.directionUnstable: A repeated single-LED comparison is unavailable or exceeds an existing exposure, alignment or image-difference limit. Check phone exposure, movement and card crops before interpreting the direction experiment.

foilCalibration.heading: Foil detection capture lab
foilCalibration.description: Experimental data collection only. Does not classify cards, change foil status, feed cards or route them.
foilCalibration.instructions: Connect and self-test the sorter, configure a webcam or paired phone above, and save camera settings. Place one known foil or non-foil card at the scanning position and keep it still. Capture ambient, white, red, green, blue and repeated white illumination. The saved lighting settings are restored afterwards.
foilCalibration.limitations: Color changes are not proof of foil. Automatic exposure, movement, sleeves and ambient light can affect results. Compare both white frames for stability. Whole-frame clipping is diagnostic only, not a foil score. Closing this tab or losing the connection can prevent lighting restoration; check the Lights page afterwards.
foilCalibration.card: Card name and printing (set / collector number)
foilCalibration.cardRequired: Enter the card name and printing (up to 200 characters).
foilCalibration.notes: Setup notes (light position, camera, sleeve, ambient light)
foilCalibration.unavailable: Requires a connected, self-tested sorter with lighting support, a ready camera, saved camera settings, available local storage and no active scan session.
foilCalibration.failed: Capture failed. No complete sample was saved. Check the camera, sorter connection and lighting alerts, then retry.
foilCalibration.cancelled: Capture cancelled. No complete sample was saved.
foilCalibration.checkLighting: Capture did not complete. Check that the previous lighting was restored.
foilCalibration.storageFailed: Local sample storage failed. Check browser storage permissions and free space.
foilCalibration.storageFull: The browser sample limit has been reached. Export and remove samples to capture more. Samples belonging to other sorters or organizations must be removed from their capture lab.
foilCalibration.saved: Labelled capture saved on this browser.
foilCalibration.storage: {{count}} samples for this sorter. Up to {{limit}} total samples across this browser. Export before removing samples or clearing browser data. Photos are not uploaded or shared across browsers.
foilCalibration.stagedSequence: Stage 1 uses configured diffused LEDs: LEDs off > normal white 32/255 > dim white 8/255 > bright white 96/255 > normal white 32/255 again. Stage 2 verifies every card: LED 0 > LED 7 > LED 0 > LED 7, each at 32/255 with the diffused LEDs off. Keep the card still and block room light. This changes LED brightness, not camera exposure; automatic exposure can compensate. The first stage does not yet classify cards or skip verification. The final experimental reading comes from the directional captures. Normal-light repeats check capture stability. Live sorting is unchanged.
foilCalibration.directionSequence: Main lighting uses configured diffused LEDs. Exposed LEDs 0 and 7 are reserved for foil detection. Keep the card still: LEDs off > diffused LEDs white 12/255 > diffused LEDs white 32/255 > LED 0 only > LED 7 only > LED 0 only > LED 7 only (single LEDs at 32/255). Requires sorter firmware with LED direction support: reflash from the website first, otherwise capture stops when the LED mask cannot be confirmed. Block room light. The foil reading is experimental.
foilCalibration.directionHelp: Direction response divides the LED {{far}} crop by the LED 0 crop pixel by pixel, so printed artwork largely cancels, then removes the smooth falloff along the strip with a 17x17 local average. Remaining sharp changes are highlights that move with the light. Repeat noise is the same measurement for LED 0 against its repeat; a useful foil signal must sit well above it. Experimental, not a foil score.
foilCalibration.directionResponse: LED 0 vs LED {{far}} ({{eligible}}% usable): 99th percentile residual {{peak}}, moving highlights {{glints}}% of card.
foilCalibration.directionNoise: Repeat noise, LED 0 vs LED 0 ({{eligible}}% usable): 99th percentile residual {{peak}}, moving highlights {{glints}}% of card.
foilCalibration.directionUnavailable: Direction comparison unavailable: missing crop or too few lit pixels.
foilCalibration.directionStability: Repeated {{led}}: intensity shift {{shift}} points; normalized difference {{difference}}%; corner shift {{movement}}% of frame diagonal.
foilCalibration.verdictMismatch: The experimental reading disagrees with the finish you selected. Check the label; if it is right, export this sample so the limits can be tuned.
foilCalibration.rainbowScore: Directional colour-change score, LED 0 vs LED {{far}}: {{first}}, repeat {{repeat}}. Broad coloured glare can also raise this score; it is not sufficient evidence of foil.
foilCalibration.localRainbowScore: Legacy local colour-change score: {{first}}, repeat {{repeat}}. Retained for comparison only; printed artwork can raise this score.
foilCalibration.normalizedScore: Artwork-normalized directional score: {{first}}, repeat {{repeat}}. Same-light noise: {{noise0}} / {{noiseFar}}. Foil requires both directional scores at or above {{foil}}; non-foil requires both at or below {{nonFoil}}. Stable, usable captures and low repeat noise are required; otherwise uncertain. Experimental, not validated accuracy or treatment recognition.
foilCalibration.normalizedCoverage: Usable directional pixels: {{eligible}}%, repeat {{eligibleRepeat}}%. Pixels responding to the light change: {{changed}}%, repeat {{changedRepeat}}%. Both require at least 25% coverage. Sleeved samples remain uncertain.
foilCalibration.reanalyzeGlare: This sample uses an older detector without artwork-normalized colour ratios. Press Analyze to update it; the old finish prediction is hidden.

page.title: Sorter setup
page.subtitle: Work through these steps in order to get a sorter ready to sort.

moduleCountStepper.label: Sorting modules
moduleCountStepper.description: How many physical sorting modules are wired up. Changes the number of bins available and the sections below.

reduceConfirm.title: Reduce module count?
reduceConfirm.description: Dropping to {{count}} modules will remove the sorting rules and calibration data for modules and bins beyond that count, across every bin preset.

detect.found: Found {{count}} module from the wired IR sensors.
detect.found_other: Found {{count}} modules from the wired IR sensors.
detect.noneFound: No IR sensors found. Check that module 1's sensor is wired.
detect.failed: Couldn't read the IR sensors from the sorter.

channelLayoutUpgrade.banner: This sorter uses the deprecated legacy channel layout, capped at 3 modules. Rewire module 1 to start at channel 0, then update to the standard layout to support up to 5 modules.
channelLayoutUpgrade.confirmDescription: Only do this after rewiring module 1 to start at PCA9685 channel 0 (module 2 at 3, module 3 at 6, feeder right after the last module). Until then, the servos will move on the wrong channels. The legacy layout can't be selected again afterwards.
channelLayoutUpgrade.done: Switched to the standard channel layout.
channelLayoutUpgrade.failed: Couldn't switch the channel layout. Try again.

experimentalFeatures.title: Experimental
experimentalFeatures.pipelinedFeedLabel: Scan the next card while sorting
experimentalFeatures.pipelinedFeedDescription: Feeds and scans the next card as soon as the previous one has left module 1, instead of waiting for it to reach its bin. Needs firmware 2.1.0 or newer and auto-feed turned on. Turn this off if cards jam or scans start picking up the moving card.

feederCalibrationPanel.heading: Feeder
feederCalibrationPanel.stopPulseDescription: The pulse where this feeder motor stands still. It differs a little from servo to servo. Adjust it until the feeder stops moving during the short preview; the speed percentages are then measured from here.
feederCalibrationPanel.speedTooltip: How fast and which way the feeder motor spins. 0% is stopped; drag either way to speed up in that direction.
feederCalibrationPanel.feedRetryCountDescription: When a feed times out without delivering a card, send the feed command again up to this many times before pausing. 0 turns retries off.
feederCalibrationPanel.settleDurationDescription: Extra time to keep feeding once the module 1 sensor sees the last card in the hopper, so it travels all the way into the mechanism before the motor stops.
feederCalibrationPanel.reverseDurationDescription: Once a card reaches module 1, spin the roller backward this long so the next card in the hopper is pulled back instead of creeping forward into a double feed. 0 turns it off.

feederTest.heading: Feeder test
feederTest.description: Feed cards straight to the bottom bin without scanning. Leave it running and adjust the feeder on the Servos & feeder page: changes apply from the next card and stay unsaved until you save.

toasts.failed: Feeder test stopped on an error. Cards sent: {{count}}

irSensorPanel.label: IR Sensors
irSensorPanel.tooltip: Infrared sensors that detect when a card is present at each module's feed path
irSensorPanel.monitorTooltip: Continuously poll the IR sensors and update the badges below in real time
irSensorPanel.readTooltip: Take a single snapshot reading of the IR sensors
irSensorPanel.detectedTooltip: A card is currently detected at Module {{module}}'s IR sensor
irSensorPanel.notDetectedTooltip: No card currently detected at Module {{module}}'s IR sensor
irSensorPanel.hopperTooltip: Whether the card hopper's IR sensor currently detects cards waiting to be fed

moduleCalibrationGrid.noPositionSelected: Select a position above to edit it
moduleCalibrationGrid.percentSliderTooltip: How far this servo is pushed, as a percent of its full range of motion. Select a position above, then drag this slider to change it - it's saved along with everything else when you hit Save.
moduleCalibrationGrid.rawPulseTooltip: Raw servo pulse position (120-490), the exact value sent to the device.
moduleCalibrationGrid.testServoTooltipGate: Test: briefly opens the gate, then returns it to closed, so you can watch it move.
moduleCalibrationGrid.testServoTooltipPusher: Test: briefly fires the pusher left, then right, then returns it to neutral, so you can watch it move both ways.
moduleCalibrationGrid.pusherOffsetWarning: More than {{percent}}% away from neutral. The arm shouldn't touch the inner wall, and the further out you push it, the higher the risk of skipping gears or the horn shifting on the shaft.
moduleCalibrationGrid.paddleOpenDelayDescription: How long the paddle gets to lower before the pusher fires. Longer if the pusher hits the card before the paddle is fully down; shorter to sort faster.
moduleCalibrationGrid.pusherHoldDurationDescription: How long the pusher stays extended before returning to neutral. Longer if cards aren't pushed fully out before it retracts; keep it short, since holding against the end stop strains the servo horn.
moduleCalibrationGrid.paddleCloseDelayDescription: How long after the pusher fires before this module's paddle closes again, independent of the pusher's own return timing. Longer if cards aren't fully clear before the gate shuts.
moduleCalibrationGrid.pushTestTooltip: Runs this module's push exactly as a route would, using the hold time and paddle close delay above (even before you save them). No card is fed; drop one onto the module first to see it pushed out.

scanRegionCalibrationPanel.instructions: Drag the box to move it, or drag the handle to resize. Line it up with a card sitting at module 1.
scanRegionCalibrationPanel.liveDetectionHint: The dashed box is the fallback crop used when live detection can't find the card - it's what you're editing. The solid outline is a live preview of what detection sees.
scanRegionCalibrationPanel.captureSettleDescription: How long to wait after the feeder confirms a card has arrived before capturing a frame, so the card is fully still and in focus.
scanRegionCalibrationPanel.matchesNeededDescription: How many consecutive frames must agree on the same card before a scan is accepted. 1 is fastest; higher values are more reliable but slower.
scanRegionCalibrationPanel.flipCameraDescription: Turn the camera picture upside down, for a camera mounted the other way round. Applies to scans and every preview of this sorter's connected camera, not to phone photos.
scanRegionCalibrationPanel.checkBothOrientationsDescription: Also match the card rotated 180°, so cards fed upside down are still identified. Turn off if all your cards are fed the same way up to make each scan faster.
scanRegionCalibrationPanel.executionProviderDescription: Which backend runs the card-matching model in your browser (card detection always runs on WASM, where it is faster). WASM is the default and works everywhere, but runs one sorter at a time. WebGPU can be faster on some GPUs, runs several sorters at once, and falls back to WASM if it fails to start.
scanRegionCalibrationPanel.regionKeyboardLabel: Scan region. Use the arrow keys to move it and the plus and minus keys to resize it. Hold Shift for bigger steps.
scanRegionCalibrationPanel.takePhotoPrompt: Take a photo from your phone to position the box.
scanRegionCalibrationPanel.phoneCaptureFailed: Phone didn't respond with a photo in time.
scanRegionCalibrationPanel.heading: Scan region

cameraPrintingScore.heading: Camera calibration aid
cameraPrintingScore.description: Choose the set, then the card on the scanner, and score one frame from the camera. Lower is closer to the stored picture of that printing. A scan accepts the card only when it is the closest match, under {{threshold}}, and clearly closer than any other card. The number is not a percentage and not a condition grade, and it can change between presses. Scoring does not change the camera and does not save anything.
cameraPrintingScore.fieldsRequired: Choose a set and a card.
cameraPrintingScore.noCollection: Choose a collection before scoring. The score uses that collection's game.
cameraPrintingScore.noCamera: Connect a camera, or take a phone photo, before scoring.
cameraPrintingScore.notSynced: That printing is not in the synced catalog for this collection's game. Sync the set, then score again.
cameraPrintingScore.nearestDifferent: The closest card in the catalog is {{name}} ({{set}} {{number}}) at {{distance}}.

verdict.accept: A scan would accept this card.
verdict.other_card: A scan would match a different card.
verdict.too_far: A scan would reject this frame. The closest card is at {{threshold}} or higher.
verdict.ambiguous: A scan would reject this frame. Another card is almost as close.
verdict.empty_index: A scan would reject this frame. No cards are synced for this game.

toasts.notCalibratedDescription: Configure all three modules before running the test sequence.
toasts.importInvalid: That file isn't a valid calibration export
toasts.saveCalibrationFailed: Failed to save the scan region or capture settle delay
toasts.pushTestUnsupported: This firmware doesn't support push tests. Update the sorter firmware.

dialog.title: Calibration differs from the sorter
dialog.description: {{name}} has calibration saved on it that doesn't match the calibration saved in the app. Choose which one to keep.
dialog.hint: Using the app's calibration overwrites the sorter's. Using the sorter's saves its values to the app, where you can still undo them from the calibration history.

toasts.adopted: Saved the sorter's calibration to the app
toasts.adoptFailed: Couldn't save the sorter's calibration, using the app's instead
toasts.storeFailed: Couldn't save calibration on the sorter

offlineCalibration.wizardBody: Nothing moves while you adjust, so you can't check these positions. The sensor check and self-test are skipped, and the saved values are sent to the sorter the next time it connects.
offlineCalibration.notConnectedBody: Connect a sorter to calibrate it live, or edit its saved calibration without one.
offlineCalibration.activeBody: Nothing moves while you adjust, so you can't check these positions. Saved values are sent to the sorter the next time it connects.
offlineCalibration.warningDescription: You can change and save this sorter's calibration without it connected, but read this first.
offlineCalibration.warningNoPreview: The servos don't move while you adjust, so you can't see whether a position is right.
offlineCalibration.warningDamage: A wrong position can drive a servo into its end stop the next time the sorter runs, which strains or strips the servo and can jam cards.
offlineCalibration.warningSync: Saved values are sent to the sorter the next time it connects. If they differ from what the sorter has stored, you'll be asked which to keep.

calibratePage.connectPi: Connect the sorter on this Pi
calibratePage.calibrateBeforeTest: Calibrate all modules before running the test
calibratePage.testBeforeControls: Run a successful test to unlock the device controls.

setupWizard.forced: Setup wizard required for this sorter
setupWizard.forcedNextConnect: It will open the next time {{name}} connects.
setupWizard.completeFailed: Couldn't save that setup is finished. Try again.
setupWizard.title: Set up your sorter

intro.heading: Let's calibrate this sorter
intro.body: Every servo stops in a slightly different place, so each position needs setting once before this sorter can run. This walks through them one at a time. Every slider moves the real servo as you drag it, so watch the sorter while you adjust.

feeder.name: Feeder
feeder.desc: The roller under the hopper that pulls one card at a time into module 1.

module.name: Modules
module.desc: The stacked sorting stages. Each one catches the card, then pushes it into one of its two bins or drops it to the module below.

bottom.name: Bottom paddle
bottom.desc: The trapdoor floor of each module. Closed holds the card, open drops it to the next module.

paddle.name: Paddles
paddle.desc: The side gates. They hold the card in place and open to let it be pushed out.

pusher.name: Pusher
pusher.desc: The arm that sweeps the card sideways into a bin.

intro.skipNote: You can skip this and calibrate later from Sorter setup.

moduleCount.heading: How many modules does this sorter have?
moduleCount.body: Count the sorting modules stacked on this sorter, not including the feeder. Each module adds two bins.

servos.bottom: The bottom paddle is the module's trapdoor floor. It holds the card while the module decides where it goes.
servos.paddle: The paddles are the side gates. They keep the card in place until it's pushed out to a bin.
servos.pusher: The pusher is the arm that sweeps the card sideways out of the module into one of its two bins.

bottomClosed.title: Bottom paddle: closed
bottomClosed.body: Drag until the trapdoor closes off the bottom of the module, so a card resting on it can't fall through. It doesn't have to be perfectly level. Stop as soon as it's closed; pushing further strains the servo.

bottomOpen.title: Bottom paddle: open
bottomOpen.body: Drag until the trapdoor swings fully open and a card would drop cleanly to the module below. Stop where it stops moving.

paddleClosed.title: Paddles: closed
paddleClosed.body: Drag until the paddles close in and hold a card in place without pinching it.

paddleOpen.title: Paddles: open
paddleOpen.body: Drag until the paddles open wide enough for a card to slide out sideways.

pusherNeutral.title: Pusher: neutral
pusherNeutral.body: Drag until the arm sits centered and clear of the card path, so cards drop straight past it.

pusherLeft.title: Pusher: left
pusherLeft.body: Drag until the arm swings toward the inner wall of the module, pushing a card out on the right side as you face the sorter. Stop before the arm touches the wall, about {{min}}-{{max}}% away from neutral. The pusher doesn't need to hit the wall to fling the card, and pressing against it strains the servo.

pusherRight.title: Pusher: right
pusherRight.body: Now the other way: drag until the arm swings toward the inner wall on the other side, pushing a card out on the left side as you face the sorter. Again, stop before it touches the wall, about {{min}}-{{max}}% away from neutral.

irSensors.heading: Check the sensors
irSensors.body: Each module has an infrared sensor at its gate that sees when a card arrives, and one more in the hopper that sees when cards are waiting. Hold a card in front of each sensor, one at a time, and watch its row light up. Each sensor gets a check once it has seen a card.
irSensors.moduleHint: Hold a card where the card rests in this module.
irSensors.hopperHint: Put a few cards in the hopper.
irSensors.waiting: Waiting for the first reading from the sorter…
irSensors.footnote: A sensor that never lights up is usually unplugged, wired to the wrong pin, or pointed away from the card path. You can continue and fix it later. If a sensor lights up with nothing in front of it, or only sees a card pressed right against it, turn the screw on its blue box (the potentiometer) until it detects a card 1 inch (2.5 cm) away.

feederStop.heading: Feeder stop point
feederStop.body: Every feeder motor has a slightly different point where it stands still. Each change runs the roller at 0% speed for a moment, so at the right stop point it doesn't move at all.
feederStop.hint: Use the buttons to step one pulse at a time.
feederStop.saveFailed: Couldn't save the feeder stop point.

guide.zero: Watch the roller after each change. This step always runs it at 0% speed.
guide.stops: Move the stop point until the roller stops moving. Note that number, for example 330.
guide.starts: Keep going the same way until the roller starts moving again. Note that number too, for example 344.
guide.middle: Set the stop point halfway between the two. For 330 and 344 that's 337.

feeder.heading: Feeder speed
feeder.body: The feeder roller pulls the bottom card out of the hopper and into module 1. Drag until it spins in the direction that pulls cards in, at a steady speed.
feeder.hint: 0% is stopped. Drag either way to spin it in that direction. It stops on its own a few seconds after you let go.

test.heading: Run the self-test
test.body: The sorter opens every trapdoor and paddle, sweeps every pusher both ways, then briefly spins the feeder. Make sure no cards are in the modules, then run it.
test.passed: Test passed. This sorter is ready to use.
test.failedHint: Go back and adjust any position that didn't move cleanly, then run the test again.

moduleDelays.heading: Timing
moduleDelays.body: These delays control how a card is pushed off this module. The defaults suit most sorters, so only change them if cards are pushed before the paddle is down or the pusher pulls back too early. Hover the info icons for what each one does.
moduleDelays.testHint: Use the push test to watch a full push with these values. It runs on an empty module.
moduleDelays.offlineHint: Push tests need a connected sorter. You can tune these later from Sorter setup.

connectionSettings.title: Connection
connectionSettings.autoConnectDescription: When this sorter is plugged in over USB while the app is open (or is already plugged in when the app loads), it connects on its own and runs its self-test so it's ready to scan. Over Bluetooth, if it drops or is power-cycled, the app keeps trying to reconnect until the tab is closed. Connect it by hand once in this browser first, so the browser allows it.
connectionSettings.testOnConnectDescription: When on, the sorter cycles every servo and checks its sensors each time it connects. When off, it only loads its saved calibration and is ready right away. You can still run the test from Sorter setup.

firmware.title: Firmware
firmware.description: Check which firmware the sorter is running and update it from this browser.
firmware.bluetoothNote: Flashing doesn't work over Bluetooth. Connect the sorter with a USB cable to flash it.
firmware.unoNote: Arduino Uno R4 boards can't be flashed from the browser. Download the firmware and upload it with the Arduino IDE.
firmware.notConnectedHint: Connect a sorter to see its version, or flash an ESP32-S3 over USB without connecting it first.
firmware.unsupported: This browser can't flash boards. Use Chrome or Edge on a computer.
firmware.cloudNote: Flashing doesn't work over Wi-Fi. Connect the sorter with a USB cable to flash it.

sectionIntros.connection: Connect the sorter over USB or Bluetooth, keep its firmware up to date and choose what happens when it connects.
sectionIntros.layout: Tell the app how many modules are installed, which slot each bin is in and how big each bin is.
sectionIntros.calibration: Fine-tune the feeder and each module's servos until cards move cleanly, then save.
sectionIntros.scanRegion: Frame the part of the camera image that holds the card, and choose how carefully each scan is matched.
sectionIntros.lights: Set the scan light's color and brightness. The sorter keeps this setting and gets it back every time the app connects.
sectionIntros.test: Check that the sensors see cards and that every bin receives them before you start sorting.

sorterModel.heading: 3D calibration
sorterModel.description: Click a marker to calibrate that part. The part you're adjusting glows and the view zooms in on its module. Your saved positions are shown as the positions the parts are designed to reach.
sorterModel.label: 3D model of the card sorter
sorterModel.hint: Drag to rotate, scroll to zoom, right-drag to pan.
sorterModel.betaDescription: Turn on to calibrate from a 3D model of the sorter: click a marker on a part to adjust it and watch it move.

drawerDescriptions.paddle: Lower the side paddles so the pusher can move a card into a side bin.
drawerDescriptions.bottom: Opens to let a card slide on to the next module.
drawerDescriptions.pusher: Pushes the card left or right off the platform.
drawerDescriptions.feeder: Feeds one card from the hopper onto module 1.

lights.previewUnavailable: Connect the sorter and pass its self-test to preview changes on the strip. You can still edit and save.

strip.heading: Light strip
strip.description: SK6812 RGBW LEDs: diffused LEDs 1 to 6, plus 8 to 15 on a 16-LED strip, provide normal lighting. Exposed LEDs 0 and 7 are for foil detection. Warnings use all configured LEDs.

lights.ledCountHelp: Choose 8 for the first board only, or 16 for both boards connected in sequence. Save to keep the setting.

off.label: Off
off.description: Normal lighting stays dark. Enabled warnings and celebrations can still light the strip.

white.label: White
white.description: Firmware 2.13+ uses the strip's dedicated neutral-white channel. Camera white balance and LED quality can still affect card colour; this is not calibrated colour.

custom.label: Custom color
custom.description: Choose an RGB color and independently set the neutral-white channel.

foil.label: Foil sweep
foil.description: A white light chases around the strip so foil cards catch the light at different angles.

celebration.heading: Valuable-card celebration
celebration.description: One LED flashes at a time from 0 to the last configured LED and back, alternating green, red and blue. Runs when a newly scanned card meets the minimum value. Disable automatic celebrations with the switch. Normal lighting returns before the next feed. Configurable strip length requires updated firmware.
celebration.previewFailed: Celebration test failed. Clear sorter alerts and update firmware for adjustable timing.
celebration.source: Uses {{source}} pricing, including foil and condition. After changing price source, save these settings again to enable celebrations for that source.
celebration.failed: The sorter did not confirm the celebration. Scanning was paused.

alerts.heading: Alerts
alerts.description: Warnings alternate with your normal center-LED lighting while a reported fault persists, stopping when its sensor clears. All times are seconds and saved per sorter. Defaults: 3 seconds warning, 5 seconds normal. Blockages take priority over an empty hopper and celebrations. Safety checks remain active when lighting warnings are disabled. Requires firmware 2.12.0.
alerts.invalidSeconds: Enter a whole number from 1 to 300 seconds.
alerts.jam: Blocked module: all configured LEDs turn red for the configured warning time.
alerts.empty: Empty hopper: all configured LEDs turn amber for the configured warning time.
alerts.value: Celebrations sweep from LED 0 to the last configured LED and back with green, red and blue flashes.

toasts.previewFailed: Lighting settings could not be confirmed. Check the sorter connection, valid timer values and firmware.
